Cyber Vault course · Module 1 · What the vault is
Unit 4 of Module 1

The vault and the Deployable Architecture are different products

By the end of this unit you'll be able to name both products, say which one this course teaches, and use the right name in a paper for Northgate's directors.

About 10 minutesNo account needed4 steps

Northgate Freight is a made-up haulier. A colleague sends Northgate's backup admin a link that says "cyber vault". Before using anything on it, the admin needs to work out which of two IBM products the link is about.

Everything this unit says about the Deployable Architecture comes from reading IBM's catalog code and docs. We never deployed it in our lab, so none of it is tested. Everything we tested in this course is IBM Cloud Cyber Vault.

Terms used. Terraform: a tool that builds cloud resources from written instructions. HMAC key: a pair of an access key ID and a secret key that object storage accepts for requests.

Step 1 · Explore the parts

Two products side by side

Both products give you a cyber vault for backups, but they're different products and they're built in different ways.

Which product is made by one API call and has two keys, one for writing and one for reading?

Show the answer

IBM Cloud Cyber Vault. IBM's docs describe it as a managed COS feature, where one call creates a hardened bucket with credentials and network rules. The Deployable Architecture is a Terraform architecture in the IBM Cloud catalog. It builds ordinary resources in the customer's account, with one HMAC key.

Which of the two did we deploy and test in our lab?

Show the answer

IBM Cloud Cyber Vault only. We never deployed the Deployable Architecture here. We decided to describe both and test the vault.

Step 2 · Predict

Whose account it's in

The biggest difference is where each product lives. Each fact below comes from IBM's own docs or catalog code. Which product does each one describe?

Fact                                                   Which product?
Sits in an account IBM manages                         ?
Builds a bucket and its services in your account       ?
Made by one create request                             ?
Made by a Terraform deployment                         ?

Which product sits in an account that IBM manages, and can't be changed after it's created?

Show the answerIBM Cloud Cyber Vault. The architecture builds everything in your own account.
Fact                                                   Which product?
Sits in an account IBM manages                         Cyber Vault
Builds a bucket and its services in your account       Deployable Architecture
Made by one create request                             Cyber Vault
Made by a Terraform deployment                         Deployable Architecture

Which product builds a bucket, network rules, a key service, Secrets Manager and logging in the customer's own account?

Show the answer

The Deployable Architecture. It's a Terraform architecture from the IBM Cloud catalog, and the customer's team looks after everything it builds. IBM Cloud Cyber Vault comes from one create request, and its bucket sits in an account that IBM manages. We read the architecture's code and didn't run it.

They also fit Data Protect differently. Data Protect locks each backup object itself. The vault can leave that to Data Protect. With its lock on, the architecture also sets a lock on the whole bucket, and Data Protect's archives don't allow that.

Step 3 · Spot the fault

A plan that belongs to the other product

A colleague at Northgate writes in a plan: "Once the cyber vault is set up, our admins can tighten its network rules whenever we need to." What's wrong with that?

What's wrong with the sentence?

Show the answer

It mixes the two products. The architecture builds its network rules in your account, so your admins can change them. IBM's overview says nothing about IBM Cloud Cyber Vault can be changed after it's created, so its allow-list has to be right on the day you create it.

When Northgate writes about these results, which name should it use?

Show the answer

IBM Cloud Cyber Vault, which is the name in our test records. You'll also see it written "IBM COS Cyber Vault". The backup software on the other side is IBM Storage Defender Data Protect 7.4.1 (Defender 2.2.1).

Watch for this. When a page or a colleague says only "cyber vault", they could mean either product. Ask which one before you reuse any number.

Step 4 · Check yourself

Three questions

Which product was tested in this course?

Show the answer

IBM Cloud Cyber Vault. We never deployed the Deployable Architecture here.

A link says "cyber vault" and describes a Terraform architecture from the IBM Cloud catalog. Which product is it about?

Show the answer

The Deployable Architecture. IBM Cloud Cyber Vault is a managed COS feature made by one API call, not a Terraform architecture.

Where does the Deployable Architecture build its bucket?

Show the answer

In your own account. That's how IBM describes it. The vault is the one that sits in an account IBM manages. We read the architecture's code, but we didn't run it.

Unit complete

You know which product is which

Your check score–Answer the three questions in step 4.
Remember

This course teaches IBM Cloud Cyber Vault. The Deployable Architecture "COS Cyber Vault for Storage Defender" is a different product. We never deployed it in our lab, and nothing in this course is a test of it. Whenever a source says only "cyber vault", ask which one it means.
